28.19: In writing. This verse literally translated reads, “He explained all in writing from the hand of Yahweh upon me, all the works of the pattern.” The LXX has a fuller reading and may be translated, “All these things in writing from the hand of the Lord David gave to Solomon according to the knowledge given to him of the work of the pattern.”

4.9: Jabez. Jabez was also the name of a town of Judah in which certain families of scribes of the lineage of Salma, the son of Hur, lived (ch. 2:50, 54, 55). More honourable than his brethren. Compare a similar phrase in Gen. 34:19.
4.10: God granted. Nothing is known of the circumstances by which God granted the earnest petition of Jabez. The important point is that God heard the prayer of faith and poured some great blessing upon His faithful servant.

10.13: Died for his transgression. This statement is not found in Samuel. It is characteristic of the writer of Chronicles, who constantly moralizes on the terrible effects of transgression and the blessings of righteousness. Which he kept not. Saul’s great sin was disobedience to the Lord’s commands (see 1 Sam. 13:13). A familiar spirit. Having failed to give heed to the Lord, Saul turned to a medium to ask guidance and counsel of demons (see on 1 Sam. 28:7–20).

21.16: Saw the angel. Compare Num. 22:31, which reports Balaam’s eyes being opened to see the angel of the Lord standing in the way. Drawn sword. The same description is given of the angel who stood in the way to intercept Balaam (Num. 22:23).
